classification.difficultyReason: Translate remainder and divisibility conditions into simultaneous linear equations for two or three unknown coefficients.

children.label: a
children.prompt: When the polynomial $P(x)=x^4-5x^3+6x^2-ax+b$ is divided by $x-3$, the remainder is 20, and when $P(x)$ is divided by $x+2$, the remainder is 30. Find $a$ and $b$.

answer.short:
$a=-14$, $b=-22$.

Use the remainder conditions to form two simultaneous equations.
answer.worked:
By the remainder theorem, $P(3)=20$ and $P(-2)=30$.
$$\begin{align*}P(3)&=81-135+54-3a+b\\P(3)&=-3a+b\\-3a+b&=20\qquad(1)\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}P(-2)&=16+40+24+2a+b\\P(-2)&=80+2a+b\\2a+b&=-50\qquad(2)\end{align*}$$
Subtracting (1) from (2),
$$\begin{align*}5a&=-70\\a&=-14.\end{align*}$$
Substituting into (1),
$$\begin{align*}-3(-14)+b&=20\\b&=-22.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find $a$ and $b$, given that the polynomial $P(x)=x^4+x^3-ax^2+bx+2$ is divisible by $x-2$ and $x-1$.

answer.short:
$a=9$, $b=5$.

Set $P(2)=P(1)=0$ and solve the resulting simultaneous equations.
answer.worked:
By the factor theorem, $P(2)=0$ and $P(1)=0$.
$$\begin{align*}P(2)&=16+8-4a+2b+2\\P(2)&=26-4a+2b\\2a-b&=13\qquad(1)\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}P(1)&=1+1-a+b+2\\P(1)&=4-a+b\\-a+b&=-4\qquad(2)\end{align*}$$
Adding (1) and (2),
$$\begin{align*}a&=9.\end{align*}$$
Substituting into (2),
$$\begin{align*}-9+b&=-4\\b&=5.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find $a$, $b$ and $c$, given that $P(x)=5x^9-ax^6+17x^4+bx^3-26x+c$ is divisible by $x$, by $x+1$ and by $x-1$.

answer.short:
$a=17$, $b=21$, $c=0$.

Use $P(0)=0$ first, then solve the equations from $P(-1)=P(1)=0$.
answer.worked:
By the factor theorem, $P(0)=P(-1)=P(1)=0$.
$$\begin{align*}P(0)&=c\\c&=0.\end{align*}$$
Using $c=0$,
$$\begin{align*}P(-1)&=-5-a+17-b+26\\P(-1)&=38-a-b\\a+b&=38\qquad(1)\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}P(1)&=5-a+17+b-26\\P(1)&=-a+b-4\\-a+b&=4\qquad(2)\end{align*}$$
Adding (1) and (2),
$$\begin{align*}2b&=42\\b&=21.\end{align*}$$
Substituting into (1),
$$\begin{align*}a+21&=38\\a&=17.\end{align*}$$
Thus $a=17$, $b=21$ and $c=0$.
